_what: Every kind of surface Trillion draws, opened once per look (scripts/check-one-look-rendered.mjs, run by scripts/deploy-worker.mjs beside the visual check, and by hand). The stand-in person wears each look in `looks`; each surface is opened in each window; the tokens a person sees are read (body background and text, the body face, the first heading's face, the primary button's fill, text and corner) and must be the SAME on every surface that wears the same look. A surface that wears a look the person did not choose (a signed-out page wears the starting look) is compared with the others wearing that look. Also refused: a picture that did not load, and a hard band (a bar pinned to the top or bottom of a scroll area, opaque, unlike the area it sits on, with no mask or gradient edge). The one-look rules (parts/screen-look/one-look-rules.json) judge the files; this judges the pixels.

tokens.primaryRadius: the primary button's corner, in pixels

anchors._what: Tokens that must also be what the worn look itself names, so every surface being wrong the same way is refused too. Each is a look variable (parts/screen-look/read-data/resolve-screen-look-palette.js).

surfaces.says: the workspace failure screen (start() rejects: the chunks it awaits answer 500)
surfaces.kept_look: a returning person: the look this device kept for the account is all the page has when the account cannot be read (workspace/main.tsx)

surfaces.says: a workspace list screen (its Add row button is the list's own action: outlined, so only its corner is compared)

read.heading: main h1, main h2, [role=tabpanel] h1, [role=tabpanel] h2, h1, h2

surfaces.says: /share/<code> for a share the stand-in made, signed out
a public page (/sign-in), which wears the starting look
the screen widget document (src/screen-view.mjs screenResources: scripts and linked sheets blocked, so the carried css alone must wear the look; its failed state is drawn into it)
surfaces.csp: script-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src data:; img-src data:

surfaces.says: an email (emailMessageHtml with the worn look's palette)
the welcome tour shell (/?tour=first-run, its Connect step)
the public site's article cards (a separate project, gettrillion.ai; opened only when --site names it)

hard_band._what: A pinned bar that is meant to read as a bar, never as a cut-off. Each row: `surface` (an id, or '*'), `match` (a regular expression over the finding), `why`.
